title: Armenia (301)
hookLine: a kingdom turns to Christ through Gregory the Illuminator, after years in a pit

cards: A man in the king's service is told to honor the king's goddess, and he says no. He's a Christian. So the king has him thrown into a deep pit under a royal fortress, and leaves him there in the dark.
Up above, time goes by and people forget him. The king assumes he's long dead.
But in the way the Armenian story is told, one person hasn't forgotten: a woman who comes to the edge and keeps him alive with food let down into the dark.

teach.b: The man's name is Gregory, and the story comes from the old Armenian history that goes under the name of Agathangelos. The king is Tiridates. While Gregory is in the pit, the king does worse.

A group of Christian women, fleeing, come to Armenia, and when one of them, Hripsime, refuses the king, he has them killed. Then, the history says, the king is struck down, his mind broken, living like a wild animal.
His sister has a dream, more than once: only Gregory can heal him. Everyone is sure Gregory is dead. They go to the pit anyway, lower a rope, and call down.
And a voice answers. They pull him out, thin and blackened, but alive. Gregory goes to the king, and the king is healed.

Gregory gathers the bones of the women who were killed and buries them with honor. He preaches, and the king who threw him in the pit is baptized. In the Armenian telling, this is the moment the kingdom turned to Christ.
Tradition points to the place, and pilgrims still go there: Khor Virap, the deep pit.
Armenians gave Gregory a name: the Illuminator, the one who brought light.

A line in the Psalms fits him almost too well, in the old King James words: "He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock." Light came up out of a hole in the ground.

how: The Armenian Apostolic Church traces its roots to the apostles Thaddeus and Bartholomew and honors Saint Gregory the Illuminator as the one who brought the faith to the kingdom and as its first chief bishop; Armenian Catholics honor him too, and pilgrims visit the monastery at Khor Virap, built over the pit where tradition says he was held.

o: a kingdom whose story turns on a man pulled from a pit
a mountain monastery where hermits lived in caves
a coastal province ruled from Rome by Constantine

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: the king who threw him in the pit
dreamed only Gregory could heal him

s: when they came to the pit, Gregory was dead
a voice answered. they pulled him out, thin and blackened, but alive.
the king who threw Gregory in the pit was later baptized
Gregory healed him, and Tiridates was baptized.
the illuminator means Gregory painted manuscripts
Armenians call him the Illuminator because he brought the light of the faith to Armenia.

games.q: you're the king's sister. you dream, again and again, that only Gregory can heal your brother. but Gregory was thrown in the pit long ago, and everyone says he's dead. what do you do?
o: forget it. the dead can't heal anyone.
go to the pit and call down.
send for a new doctor instead.
games.why: they went to the pit and lowered a rope, and a voice answered. Gregory came up alive, and healed the king.

practice: Picture the people of Armenia, and Armenians living far from it, carrying their own church and their own alphabet with them: a family at a table, a church on a hill, a grandmother lighting a candle.
Then let your mind rest on anyone you know who is in a pit right now, the kind no one else sees. If you pray, pray for Armenia and for them; if not, hold them in the light.

wordCard.voice: Armenia. The kingdom whose story turns on a man in a pit, pulled out alive, who became Gregory the Illuminator.

orig.note: Armenian: the deep pit, the name of the place where tradition says Gregory was held.

carryVoice: Your line: light from a pit. A rope went down, and a voice answered. That's day seven hundred ninety-six.
